findings.element: render-b.js — the step() closure inside editor() ("focus: function () { event.currentTarget.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }") and undo() at line 532
findings.problem: The one entry on the undo stack that carries a focus closure is the primary gesture's, and that closure reads event.currentTarget after the dispatch has finished, when the browser has already nulled it. Every undo of a move throws "Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'focus')" — reproduced at 390, 768, 1152, 1279, 1280 and 1440, one throw per press. The throw lands between paintUndo() and "window.scrollTo(0, top.at)", so the line that exists specifically to give the owner their place back never executes. Measured at 1440 from owner-editing: .b-measureHead top is -49 at the press, the owner scrolls 700px away to -749, presses Undo — the moment moves back and the view stays at -749. At 390 the same run goes 219 to -285, half a screen from the thing that just changed. The delete entry carries no focus closure, does not throw, and restores the view to the pixel (219 to 219, -49 to -49), so the reversibility surface honours its promise for the action an owner takes once and breaks it for the action they take all day. The behaviour gate's "undo returns focus to the control that made the change" passes only by accident: it presses Ctrl+Z while focus is already sitting on the .b-step it just clicked, so the assertion is satisfied by the exception aborting before anything moves. "zero console errors" is only ever measured on a fresh load, never after a press.
findings.fix: In step(), capture the button in the handler rather than in the closure: at the top of the click handler add "var pressed = event.currentTarget;" and change the remembered entry to "focus: function () { pressed.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }". In undo(), make the place restore unconditional and ordered first: move "if (typeof top.at === 'number') window.scrollTo(0, top.at);" above the focus call and wrap the focus call in try/catch so no future closure can eat it again. Then add to interaction-check.mjs, in the reversibility block, an assertion that pushes the page 700px off after a move and requires .b-measureHead to return to within 2px after Undo, and a second that fails the run if any pageerror fires during the whole interactive suite, not only at load.

findings.element: render-b.js keepInBand() — the early return "if (!panel || getComputedStyle(panel).position !== 'fixed') return;" — as it applies to the .b-step buttons and the add action at 1280 and 1440
findings.problem: keepInBand is gated on the editor being a fixed sheet, so at 1280 and above — the width an owner actually plans at — nothing ever follows the object being changed. Driven from owner-editing at 1440x960: the edited row's .b-copy opens at top 696, one press of +7 puts it at 822, the second at 948 (below the fold), and it keeps going to 1704 after eight presses while window.scrollY never leaves 0. The owner goes on pressing a stepper for a moment that left the screen two presses ago; the only surviving feedback is the mono readout inside the panel, which is a sentence — the exact thing this direction chose position over. Add is worse: scrolled to 900 at 1440, "Add a moment" inserts the new row at top -456, 456px above the viewport, and drops focus into a title field for a moment the owner has never seen. At 390 all three behave correctly because the sheet is fixed there, so the primary gesture has two different characters depending on width and the weaker one is the owner's. The comment defending the early return says the scroll path would move the steppers under the hand — it would not: .b-stick computes position: sticky at these widths, and I watched the first .b-step hold while the page scrolled from 0 to 1200.
findings.fix: Delete the position check from keepInBand and derive the free edge instead: "var fixed = panel && getComputedStyle(panel).position === 'fixed'; var free = fixed ? panel.getBoundingClientRect().top - 16 : window.innerHeight - 16;" and leave the rest of the function as written; guard only on the panel existing. Call keepInBand from the add branch of wireOwner, on the same requestAnimationFrame, after openEditor and before the input focus, so a created moment is brought into the band the way a moved one is. Then widen the gate's "the move is on screen where it happens" loop from [390, 768] to every viewport in the config, and add "the moment just added is on screen" measured the same way.

findings.element: state=loading-slow — act("Try again", false, { "data-act": "retry" }) at render-b.js line 1545
findings.problem: There is no handler for data-act="retry" anywhere in render-b.js; grep returns exactly one hit, the line that draws the button. Driven at 390x844: press it and nothing at all changes — body text identical, .b-field keeps aria-busy="false", .b-live stays empty, no skeleton returns, no visual acknowledgement of any kind, and three seconds later it is still the same frame. This is the only control on the only screen where the audience meets failure: a phone, in the evening, the plan not arriving. A guest presses it, gets no answer, and has no way to tell whether the product tried. The gate's "and offers a way on" counts the button's existence (slow.way === 1), and the "every control does something" loop, which presses every button and checks that something changed, runs over owner-flight, owner-empty, owner-editing, publish, phone, desk and day — loading-slow and ended are both outside it, which is why an inert button and a screen with zero focusable elements both pass.
findings.fix: Wire retry in the guest branch the way copy is wired: on press, set .b-field aria-busy="true", swap the stalled block back to the loading frame's own markup (the .b-skel run plus "Bringing in what is ahead."), write "Trying again." into .b-live, keep focus on the button, and after the declared 0.22s easing plus the fixture's stall delay restore the stalled face with .b-live set to "Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works." Add loading-slow and ended to the state list in the gate's "every control does something" loop, and tighten that loop so a change confined to document.activeElement.className no longer counts as the control having done something.

findings.element: .b-copy margin-top: var(--push) against .b-tick / .b-away, which stay on the true pixel (b.css lines 199-215)
findings.problem: When two moments fall closer than a row is tall, the words are pushed clear but the tick and the count are not, and nothing is drawn joining a mark to the words it belongs to. Driven at 1440 from owner-editing: five presses of −1 move "Send the invitations" from 23 days to 18, and the result is a mark and a count reading 18 painted at y 608-612, level with "Sat 1 Aug" — the date line of the moment above it — while the title it names, "Send the invitations / Mon 3 Aug", sits 76px lower against blank track. Screenshot captured. A reader scanning the gutter reads 16 against "Menu tasting at The Orchard" and 18 against "Sat 1 Aug", which is the wrong date for that count. It compounds: after five presses of Add — the ordinary way an owner starts filling a plan, since add always lands at max(1, first ahead − 7) — the copy for the moment at 2 days sits 266px below its own tick, with two other moments' words in between. Same-day moments are handled properly (data-stack lead/follow hides the duplicate mark and rules the rows together), so the mechanism for saying "these belong together" already exists; it simply stops at exactly one day apart. The gate measures collisions on .b-copy only, never on .b-tick or .b-away, so the whole class is invisible to it.
findings.fix: In place(), when a row's computed --push is greater than 2px, set data-pushed="true" on the .b-item and write the push distance to a --lead custom property. In b.css add ".b-item[data-pushed='true']::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: -20px; top: 10px; width: 1px; height: calc(var(--lead) - 4px); background: var(--fore-16); }" so a hairline runs down the gutter from the mark to the top of its own copy, and move .b-away down with the copy by giving it "margin-top: var(--push, 0px)" while the tick stays on the true pixel — the tick is the position, the count is a label on the words. Assert in the gate that for every row the vertical distance between .b-away and the top of its own .b-copy is under 4px, at 390 and 1440, after twenty step presses and after five adds.

findings.element: .b-edit { padding-top: 88px } with .b-edit .b-undo[data-empty="true"] { display: flex; visibility: hidden } (b.css lines 815-831)
findings.problem: Every editor open begins with a hole. Measured at 390x844: the sheet spans y 254-832 and the first thing in it, the "WHAT IT IS" label, sits at 343 — 89px of nothing across the full 366px width, 15% of a 578px sheet on the screen where room is scarcest. At 1440 the same 88px sits at the top of a panel that is otherwise the only thing in a column with 600px of empty below it. The reserve is right — the steppers must not move when the undo bar fills — but the band is spent on nothing, and the panel it heads has no visible name at all: aria-label="Editing Send the invitations" exists for the accessibility tree, and a sighted owner is told which moment they are editing only by reading the value out of the title field. On the phone the sheet covers four other rows' controls, so the panel is most of what is on screen and it opens anonymous.
findings.fix:
Render a sibling of .b-undo inside the same absolute box — "

Editing

" positioned absolute top:16 left:16 right:16 like the bar, the label in the mono micro register at --fore-62 and the value at --size-body --fore — and swap the two by the same data-empty flag: .b-edit[data-undo] .b-editName { visibility: hidden } and .b-edit .b-undo[data-empty='true'] { visibility: hidden } as now, so the band is always occupied and its geometry never changes. Populate it in editor() from nameOf(record) and update it in setTitle() alongside the aria-label it already rewrites, so a rename reaches both. Assert in the gate that at every viewport the topmost visible text inside .b-edit names the moment being edited before any change is made.

biggestWin: The keyboard model is real, complete for everything it advertises, and it holds together: eleven tab stops on the whole owner surface, the entire row as the target rather than the badge (an ::after at inset 0 that elementFromPoint confirms over the title), Enter and Space open the editor, Escape closes it and returns focus to the row that opened it, Ctrl Z is named on the face of the control and stays out of the way inside a text field, the undo surface is one node that travels to wherever the change is being made, delete restores both focus and the exact scroll, the sheet's band is reserved in real layout (602px of padding at 390, nothing stranded under it, no internal scroll), every thumb target on the phone is 44px, and the row control is drawn at rest rather than revealed on hover so there is no discoverability problem anywhere in the product. What stands between this and 9.5 is not a redesign. It is one build of about a day and a half plus one small decision. The build: fix the null currentTarget so undo stops throwing and starts restoring the view, and delete the position check in keepInBand so the moment being moved or created is brought on screen at 1280 and 1440 the way it already is at 390 — those two together are the difference between an instrument whose central claim is that position is the quantity and one where, at the width the owner plans at, the quantity leaves the screen after two presses and the undo that would bring it back throws an exception on the way. The decision, and it is the smaller one: what a mark means when the words it belongs to have been pushed away from it, and whether the count follows the words or stays on the true pixel. Everything else on this list is polish measured in hours.
